title: First time developing a game with AI (or without it!). Please, help me!
author: Tenofaz
selftext:
Hi, everyone.

I’m developing a game that simulates a D&D-based TTRPG—or rather, it simulates the Dungeon Master and the game table.  
The actual players still need to meet up to play together around a computer running this software.  
This is my first time trying to develop a game (with or without AI), and I’m using Anthropic’s Claude for this project.

I wanted to ask you all whether, in your opinion, the way I’m designing the game and using Claude is correct, or if different approaches would allow me to work more efficiently.  
Basically, in Claude Code for Desktop, I’ve created 5 or 6 different sessions within the same project—all Worktree sessions—that almost always run on Sonnet 5.5 medium/high.  
I oversee everything, with help from Claude Opus 5.5 in a separate Chat/Cowork project.  Let’s say this acts as a “consultant.”  It can’t intervene directly, but it shares suggestions with me on how to make the various Claude Code sessions work.  
The 5–6 Code sessions each cover different aspects of the game:  the rules and adventure engine, the narrator and his voice, the game interface and game board, the 3D models, and the game manual.  
I’ve also had a Fable 5.2 session run through the entire game once or twice to review the graphics and code.

Do you think this is an effective and efficient system? Do you have any suggestions on how to improve it, or are there things that should be changed?

  
A big thank you in advance to anyone who would like to contribute!
